budget_rationale: b03's sizing: one milestone confined to two static files plus one test, with no server change. A frontend order has no measured economics here, so the smallest measured sizing applies.
goal: In the sample project, add an item-count badge to the items widget: the served page gains an element with id item-count, and the script fills it from the /items response with '1 item' for one item, 'N items' otherwise, and 'No items yet' for an empty list, through a pure countLabel(n) function it exports beside renderItems. Judge it at the HTTP level: the served page and script carry the badge, and the service's suite is green.

dod: GET /widget serves a page containing an element with id item-count
GET /static/widget.js serves a script that defines and exports countLabel and writes its result into item-count
countLabel(0), countLabel(1) and countLabel(3) return 'No items yet', '1 item' and '3 items'
tests/test_api.py pins the served badge and stays green
no file outside benchproj/web/ and tests/test_api.py changed
milestones.title: Count badge served and wired

rationale: The frontend-widget capability, written against the bench's own fixture because the gauntlet's sample project holds no web asset (R-0411, DECISION F082 D3). F082's Design judges it by build plus the HTTP-level smoke with no browser dependency, and the fixture serves the widget page at /widget and its script at /static/widget.js so that smoke exists before the mission starts. Premise, checked by the bench's own test: neither the served page nor the served script mentions item-count or countLabel today, so the badge is genuinely absent; the script already separates the pure renderItems from the page-touching load, so the order asks the mission to follow a shape the file already shows.
title: Add a count badge to a static widget served over HTTP
